summary: Prefetch handshake stall during multipart streaming splits model pin and causes mixed-variant responses
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled canary weight increase for a dedicated customer (Lexicon Health) we observed multipart streaming requests that triggered a prefetch handshake to stall. Some sessions completed the handshake and retained a pinned model variant while others fell back to the baseline variant, causing mixed-variant responses for a single user session.

Impact:
- Several customer API calls returned inconsistent model behavior (different answer styles and tokenization) within the same conversation session.
- Customer reported degraded user experience for ~2% of requests in the affected cohort; no data loss reported.
- Billing spike observed due to unexpected re-runs on client side (~$220 additional tokens within the window).

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster for Lexicon Health in prod-us-west
- Rolling canary: target weight increased from 10% to 30% at 2026-03-10T02:15:00Z
- Models involved: redwood-open-7b-v2 (canary variant), redwood-open-1.3b (baseline)
- Edge and prewarm services: prewarm-service v2.11.0, edge-cache v1.9.1

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Send multipart streaming payloads (large prompt + attachments) pinned to the tenant route during a gradual canary weight increase.
2) Observe long-running prefetch handshake for KV cache warmup (timeouts between controller and prewarm-service).
3) During handshake stall, routing logic sometimes returns fallback route to baseline variant instead of waiting for pin commit.
4) Client receives first tokens from baseline; subsequent partial handshake completion rebinds subsequent requests to canary -> mixed responses.

Logs / Evidence:
- Edge request traces: trace ids available in comments below (e.g., trace: usw-req-20260310-7f2b4)
- Prewarm service logs: repeated "handshake: waiting on kvcache-warmup" followed by "handshake aborted: prewarm-timeout" for affected sessions.
- Orchestrator snapshot: commit for canary cohort delayed by 12s then partially applied on a subset of shards.

Initial hypothesis:
- Prefetch handshake timeout setting (default 10s) is too aggressive for multipart streaming with large attachment KVs; when handshake times out the routing fallback path is incorrectly taking precedence and not preserving explicit pin intent for in-flight sessions.
- Race between prewarm acknowledgment and edge routing cache eviction causes some requests to observe stale routing metadata.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced in staging by increasing multipart size and lowering prewarm timeout; observed same split behavior when handshake delay >8s.
- Traced request flow across edge -> prewarm -> orchestrator; observed orchestrator returning partial commit ack to some shards while others still report prewarm in progress.
- Orchestrator commit logic treats partial shard commit as success for route selection in the edge cache. This causes early routing decisions for subsequent requests.
- No evidence of tenant cookie corruption; session tokens were consistent.

Temporary mitigation applied (2026-03-11 04:30 UTC):
- Increased prewarm handshake timeout to 30s for Lexicon Health dedicated cluster to reduce aborts.
- Adjusted edge routing to prefer existing session affinity when handshake state is pending (suppress fallback-to-baseline for in-flight pinned sessions).

Resolution plan / next steps:
1) Engineering (serving-runtime) to add stronger guard: do not treat partial shard commit as route-commit until all shard acknowledgments are received or a deterministic quorum is met. (PR drafted, see linked PR).
2) Prewarm team to implement progressive backoff for KV warmup when multipart attachments are detected and surface warmup progress to orchestrator.
3) Edge caching: add short grace period for session-affinity preservation while handshake pending.
4) Post-incident: run a controlled canary with large-multipart test vectors to validate heuristics.

Customer communication:
- Notified Lexicon Health CS contact with interim mitigations and ETA for full fix. Customer asked for a postmortem and permanent fix timeline.

root_cause: Race between prewarm handshake timeout and orchestrator partial shard commit; orchestrator treating partial shard ack as route commit caused routing divergence and fallback to baseline variant mid-session.
